E10_xpath_baseline.note: A8 is our own XPath-subset re-implementation reading element types, link targets and visible text; not ATUSA or Crawljax; the authors knew the labels; ordering of writing vs. first run is an authorial statement the artifact cannot evidence

derivation.readme_sentence: Guest users must never see administrative links, nor should they be able to access administrative pages.
derivation.derivation_notes: README names the dashboard sidebar link 'Admin Dashboard' as the UI violation. Reaching admin.html is described as a backend-enforcement violation, which an element-level clause cannot express, so it yields no triple. The README is silent about links on other pages; any other finding is scored as a false positive and discussed.

derivation.readme_sentence: Every page on first load must display a cookie consent banner or modal, regardless of user role.
derivation.derivation_notes: One page, one required clause, banner documented as absent.

control_with_banner_inserted.note: A8's queries include the inserted markup by construction; the informative part is whether A3 can ever stop firing

missing-consent-demo.A8_row_note: Any absence-based clause scores 1/1 on a page without a banner, so this row does not discriminate between arms for A8; the control is circular for A8.

derivation.readme_sentence: Free Tier users must never see or interact with Premium features, specifically the Export Data functionality (policy text also names an Advanced Analytics panel).
derivation.derivation_notes: README documents only the Export Data button as the violation. If the page also shows an analytics panel, that finding is README-ambiguous: it is scored as a false positive under this README-derived truth and flagged; a truth variant that includes it is also reported.

truth_variant_with_named_analytics_panel.note: A8's exact-heading query misses the analytics panel, so A8 is 1 of 2 under this truth

E12_extra_apps.disclosure: Same-project apps; tiny, single-defect, unannotated (no data-tag). Static HTML audited per page; no crawl, browser or service. Ground truth derived from README sentences first; ordering is an authorial statement the artifact cannot evidence. The XPath invariants were written after reading the scored HTML, so A8 results here are in-sample. Nothing under test-apps/ is modified.

protocol.ordering: Self-attested: invariants were written from policy.txt and policy.expected.json (and directory file names) before any .html, ground_truth.json or README.md of these apps was opened. The artifact cannot prove this; the hash and timestamp only show the invariants file did not change afterwards.
protocol.a3_subjects: verbatim 'subject' strings of policy.expected.json, no tuning
protocol.provenance: Same-project, AI-generated (fixture-forge), unannotated (no data-tag); they add variety and a more blind protocol, not independence.
protocol.scoring: TP = found triple in ground_truth violations. FP = found triple on a page listed in clean_pages for that clause. unlisted = found on a page in neither list (reported, not counted as FP). FN = ground-truth violation not found. decoy_adjacent = FP on a clean page whose visible text contains a content word (>=4 letters, not in a small stoplist) of the clause subject (mechanical definition fixed before running).
